hero.kicker: Who do you put on air?
hero.headline: {models} narrator models. {fixtures} rigged fixtures. One fixed referee.
hero.how: Every model commentates the same seeded matches, each with planted traps. Code checks every number and name. A second model checks the wording. Nothing a model says counts until it survives review.
hero.trapDef: A trap is a planted moment where a plausible sentence is wrong.

table.auditorNote: Most accurate when it answered, but missed {held} of {claims} moments and takes {s} s per claim. Also the auditor.
table.incompleteNote: Not ranked: missed more than 1 in 10 moments
table.key: Clean: stood with no fix. Referees split: the judge and the auditor disagreed. Fail profile: what the failed claims got wrong, as a share of them.

footer.relegationBody: More OVERTURNED than AMENDED: not cleared for air.
footer.rerunBody: Same six seeds, same referee. When a vendor ships an update, the table runs again.

fixtures.title: The exam paper. Six seeded matches. Each one plants a trap.
fixtures.refereeNote: The referee is fixed: code checks every number and name, then a judge and an auditor read the wording. Every narrator sits the same paper.
fixtures.how: A fixture is a seed and a plan: the moments the match must contain, such as a red card on the hour or a stoppage-time penalty. The generator plays it out, so every narrator sees the same events and the same facts.
fixtures.stamp: STANDS: the claim matches the facts. AMENDED: the wording was fixed. OVERTURNED: the claim was withdrawn, cited a fact that doesn't exist, could not be read, or was never written. HELD: the model call failed, so there is no answer; it scores 0.
fixtures.trapMoment: Stamp on the first trap moment
fixtures.gridNote: Each cell shows how that narrator called this fixture's {traps} traps (the other moments are on Compare). S is STANDS, A is AMENDED, O is OVERTURNED, H is HELD. Click a stamp to see the claim next to the others.

compare.headline: Same moment. {n} narrators. One referee.
compare.note: Prose is not ranked. Only what failed is highlighted.
compare.badCitation: cited a fact that does not exist
compare.refereeNote: Code reconciles every number and name against the fact registry before any model reads the sentence. The judge and the auditor only judge wording.
compare.fixtureLink: See the fixture this came from
